subject: Renewal restructure: staggered onramp + co-terming for Starlit Health
messages:
From: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@starlithealth.com>

Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@starlithealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal inquiry — term restructure & staged onramp

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. Our annual renewal with Redwood is coming up and we’re exploring a restructure that better matches our product rollout across environments. High level:

- Looking to commit to a 36-month term (multi-year) to lock pricing and secure capacity.
- We want a staged onramp: 30% year 1, 50% year 2, 100% year 3 (by token volume/throughput).
- We have two existing Redwood contracts and would prefer to co-term them to a single renewal date.
- We need clarity on auto-renew: our procurement team prefers an opt-out (no auto-renew), but we understand that may affect pricing.

Can you share options (pricing tiers, credit/true‑up mechanics, billing cadence) and any constraints on co-terming? I’ve attached our Q3 usage export for reference.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if it helps.

—Derek
Derek Shaw

Kim/Team — quick guidance before the customer call:

- Pricing cadence suggestion (tiered by year): Year 1 = 12% off list; Year 2 = 8% off list; Year 3 = 4% off list. That lands roughly in the 22–24% blended discount depending on weighting (we can tighten based on final volumes).
- Auto-renew opt-out: approve only with a 2% premium (applied year-over-year) or a contract clause that requires 30 days’ written notice plus a 60‑day wind‑down credit window. Legal must sign off, so include that ask in the SOW.
- Co-term migration: Ops (Camila) — please confirm migration window. Avoid billing overlap and ensure we can backfill prefix caches during cutover. If they require a hard cutover, add a one‑time migration credit.

Approve presenting the above as a ‘balanced’ option; present a higher‑discount aggressive option only if Derek signals consolidation urgency.

—Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

Attached is a quick model (tabbed): gross list, proposed discounts, Year1/Year2/Year3 volume splits, and cashflow by quarter. Notes:

- Using reported Q3 usage as baseline, Year1 = 0.3 * final target; Year2 = 0.5; Year3 = full.

Subject: Proposed renewal structure — Starlit Health (36‑month laddered onramp)

Hi Derek — thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion, please find the proposed structure below and next steps. Attached: Starlit_Renewal_Proposal_20261014.pdf, SOW_amendment_draft.docx.

Summary (proposal A — balanced):
- Term: 36 months, effective upon signed SOW amendment.
- Ramp: Year1 = 30% of committed capacity; Year2 = 50%; Year3 = 100% (true‑up at each anniversary).
- Pricing: Year1 = 12% off list; Year2 = 8% off list; Year3 = 4% off list. True‑up mechanics described in SOW (annual reconciliation).
- Co‑terming: We will consolidate the two existing contracts to a single co‑term. Billing will be unified; migration window and data cutover scheduled in the SOW. One‑time migration credit applied in Year1.
- Auto‑renew: We can support an opt‑out (no automatic renewal) subject to: (a) a 2% premium applied across the term OR (b) an alternate commitment floor (minimum annualized spend at 50% of Year1 projected). Legal will need to review the opt‑out clause.
- Operational guarantees: burst lanes and prefix cache backfill will be provisioned; Camila will confirm a 48–72 hour cutover window.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached proposal and SOW draft.
2) If acceptable, sign the SOW draft and we’ll route to Legal for the auto‑renew clause.
3) Camila will set a migration runbook and schedule the co‑term cutover.

Would you like us to issue a redlineable DocuSign version of the SOW? If so, we’ll generate it and loop Legal.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this locked.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
